the solid dispersions of ITR in superdisintegrant excipients, especially Ac-Di-Sols, can enhance the dissolution rate of the drug.
solid dispersions of itranconazole in superdisintegrant excipients can be used to formulate fast disintegrating tablets with improved dissolution rate.
solid dispersions in the superdisintegrant, Ac-Di-Sal, gave the best dissolution enhancement of ITR and the corresponding tablets were formulated and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dissolution enhancement of ITR using superdisintegrants.
the development of a novel approach for the enhancement of dissolution of poorly soluble drugs.
the development of a solid dispersion technique to enhance the dissolution of a poorly water-soluble drug.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
superdisintegrants are the most suitable excipients for enhancing the dissolution rate and dissolution efficiency of ITR from the solid dispersions.
solid dispersions of itrocanazole in superdisintegrant excipients are a promising approach to enhancing the dissolution rate and hence the bioavailability of poorly water-soluble drugs such as ITR.
solid dispersion in superdisintegrant is the best approach to enhance the dissolution of ITR.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the solid dispersions of ITR in superdisintegrant excipients and their formulation into tablet form could be used for enhancing the dissolution rate and DE values of ITR.
the solid dispersions in the superdisintegrant Ac-Di-SOL are the best for the dissolution enhancement of itraconzole.
solid dispersions in the superdisintegrant Ac-Di-Sal gave the highest improvement in the dissolution rate and the best tablet formulations of ITR.
The main takeaway from our work is that
superdisintegrants can act as a good carrier for the preparation of solid dispersions of drugs that have poor aqueous solubility and dissolution rates.
superdisintegrants can be used as carriers for the preparation of solid dispersion formulations.
solid dispersions of drugs in superdisintegrant excipients can be used to enhance their dissolution rate.
